overview: The Medford City Council met to address various local resolutions, licensing petitions, and ordinance updates. Key actions included referring parking meter adjustments to a Committee of the Whole, endorsing state dyslexia screening legislation, and approving a special permit for a new business.

items.title: Public Hearing on Special Permit for 375 Riverside Ave
items.summary: The Council approved a special permit for 375 Riverside Avenue, LLC to operate retail sales for a hair threading spa, subject to traffic light timing review, sidewalk repairs, and entrance/exit signage.

items.title: Resolution on Hegner Center Property Transfer
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution requesting the mayor begin negotiations with Bridgewell to return the Hegner Center building to city ownership for potential use as an arts center.

items.title: Claim Expenditure Approval for Sewer Damage
items.summary: The Council approved a $2,637.71 claim settlement to Frances Souza for property damage caused by a city sewer backup.

items.title: Resolution on Business District Parking Meters
items.summary: The Council referred a proposal to replace parking kiosks with single-head meters in business districts to a Committee of the Whole meeting with the mayor and Republic Parking.

items.title: Resolution Supporting Dyslexia Screening Legislation
items.summary: The Council endorsed state legislation for early dyslexia screening in public schools and directed the resolution to state representatives, the School Committee, and the Superintendent.

items.title: Resolution Regarding Porta-Potty Fees for Youth Sports
items.summary: The Council requested a report from the health department and mayor's office on the fee structures, permitting, and potential city cost-sharing for porta-potties at city parks.

items.title: Condolence Resolutions
items.summary: The Council expressed condolences to the families of Stacey K. Kirkpatrick and Brendan Daddario and observed a moment of silence.

items.title: Common Victualler License for Two Chins Restaurant
items.summary: The Council approved a common victualler license transfer for Two Chins Restaurant, Inc., operating as Maylings at 434A Salem Street.

items.title: Public Input on Public Safety Facility Needs
items.summary: Resident Jeanne Martin urged the administration and public to prioritize building a modern public safety facility, and her petition was placed on file.

items.title: Outdoor Dining Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: The Council approved the first reading of an amendment clarifying that the outdoor dining ordinance applies strictly to sidewalk property under city jurisdiction.

items.title: Public Input on Lawrence Memorial Hospital Status
items.summary: Following concerns raised by resident Rob Cappucci, the Council approved a motion asking the administration to inquire with Hallmark Health about the potential sale of Lawrence Memorial Hospital.

items.title: Resolution Congratulating Medford Night Event Organizer
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution commending Jay Campbell for organizing a Medford Night fundraising event at a Boston Celtics game.

items.title: Report Request on Common Victualler Licenses
items.summary: The Council approved a motion requesting an administrative report on outstanding common victualler licenses and Board of Health inspection delays.

items.title: Request for Missing Republic Parking Attachments
items.summary: The Council requested that Republic Parking re-send its response regarding a prior paper along with the missing attachments.

items.title: Public Input on Senior Parking Discounts
items.summary: Resident Robert Penta raised concerns about promised senior parking discounts, prompting the Council to include the topic in their upcoming parking meeting with the mayor.
